clue.text: Racing driver somewhere in Scotland facing simple plant

indicators.note: facing puts the town up against the plant, one beside the other

parts.note: Stirling is a city in central Scotland
moss is a simple, flowerless plant

explanation.surface: A racing driver turns up in a Scottish spot, standing opposite some humble plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Stirling Moss was a celebrated British Formula One driver of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Stirling Moss is one of the best-known British motor-racing drivers ever.

clue.text: Cherished walk around firm

indicators.note: around says the walk goes round the outside of the firm word

parts.note: to tread is to walk
firm, as in certain, means sure

explanation.surface: Someone takes a beloved stroll around a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but here it is the adjective meaning certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is held dear, valued highly like a precious possession.

clue.text: Wine held by barman is termed uplifting

indicators.note: uplifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
held by says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pub server's description is cheering, and wine is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Wine held' as the definition, but 'held by' is the signal that the letters sit in 'barman is termed'; the definition is just 'Wine'. ANISTER, read upwards in this down clue, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Batting partner who's doing a stretch

parts.note: in cricket a side that is batting is 'in'
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A cricketer's batting partner turns out to be serving a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing a stretch' is slang for serving time in prison, not limbering up.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner, someone serving a term behind bars.

clue.text: Visitors ignoring temperature estimate

indicators.note: ignoring says the temperature letter is left out of the visitors word

parts.note: guests are visitors

explanation.surface: Guests who pay no attention to the thermometer make a rough estimate.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to estimate without full information; both are synonyms here as verbs or nouns.

clue.text: Lofts stripped frequently

indicators.note: stripped means the word Lofts loses its outer letters, keeping only the inside

explanation.surface: Attics are often cleared out.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is an old or poetic word for often.

clue.text: Small nucleus with these distributed record of game

parts.note: a core is a nucleus or centre

indicators.note: distributed says the letters of these are spread around into a new order

explanation.surface: Sounds like a physics note about a little nucleus and things spread around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoresheet is the form on which the scores of a match are recorded.

clue.text: Departed from port

definitions.meaning: the past tense of leave, so departed
port is the ...-hand side of a ship, so from port means on the ...

explanation.surface: A ship sailed away from the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbour, but it is the left side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Left means went away, and also the side named port at sea.

clue.text: Accomplished musician excited Tom's ear

indicators.note: excited suggests letters stirred up and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A gifted musician thrills Tom's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially a great conductor or performer.

clue.text: Unorthodox climbers might fall thus

definitions.meaning: an idiom for eccentric or unconventional
a rock climber who slips comes literally off the climbing wall

explanation.surface: Odd climbers might take a tumble this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-wall is informal for bizarre or unconventional; climbers literally drop off a wall.

clue.text: Authoritarian Conservative is brought in quickly

indicators.note: brought in says the Conservative and is are placed inside the quickly word

parts.note: fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A political tyrant: a Tory is rushed into place.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascist supports authoritarian, dictatorial nationalist rule.

clue.text: Mark's overcome by a certain World War One battle

indicators.note: overcome by says the mark letter is covered, sitting inside the a certain word

parts.note: some, as in 'some person', means a certain
M stands for mark, the old German currency; the 's is 'is' joining the parts

explanation.surface: Mark is beaten by someone at a famous First World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme, in northern France, saw one of the bloodiest battles of 1916.

clue.text: Old European explorer hurt fellow on equestrian pursuit

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first part above the next

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or hurt
co- is the prefix for a fellow, as in co-worker
polo is a sport played on horseback

explanation.surface: A colleague was injured on horseback in a polo match.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller who journeyed to China in the 13th century.

clue.text: Headwear initially tested in the city

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of tested

parts.note: urban means in or of the city

explanation.surface: A new hat is first tried out in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a head covering made of cloth wound round the head.

clue.text: Formality of celebrity and Companion of Honour

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Stiff manners from a famous person who also holds an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British award given for major achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch means stiff, prim formality of manner, from the stiffening used on linen.

clue.text: Ring pub, finding traffic obstruction

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Phoning the pub reveals there's a roadblock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is a bell tolling.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll bar is a barrier across a road where travellers must pay to pass.

clue.text: Train group of dolphins

definitions.meaning: a group of fish or marine mammals such as dolphins

explanation.surface: Teaching a pod of dolphins tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: School is both a verb for instruction and a collective noun for sea creatures.

clue.text: Duck's colour that is reflected

indicators.note: reflected says the letters come back as in a mirror, read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A duck's plumage colour shows in its reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, famous for its soft down.

clue.text: Arena's gymnastic equipment

definitions.meaning: a ring is an arena, as in a boxing or circus ring
a pair of hanging hoops used in gymnastics

explanation.surface: A stadium's gymnastics apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: As a definition of the plural answer, 'Arena' stands for arenas; the 's is 'is' joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings are both fighting or circus enclosures and the hoops gymnasts swing on.

clue.text: Charlie, unaccompanied, eating unknown Italian food

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: eating says the alone word swallows the unknown letter

parts.note: unaccompanied means alone
z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Charlie dines alone on some mystery Italian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A calzone is a folded pizza, a pocket of dough filled with cheese and meat.

clue.text: Worker on Iago, heartless character in Shakespeare

parts.note: a worker is an ant, as in worker ant

indicators.note: heartless means Iago loses its middle letters, leaving only its two ends

explanation.surface: A worker turns on the cruel Iago, himself a Shakespearean villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago is the villain of Othello, adding to the Shakespeare picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is a name used for several Shakespeare characters, notably the merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Greek character's teacup regularly avoided

indicators.note: regularly avoided means every other letter of teacup is skipped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A Greek person keeps steering clear of the teacup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character's' reads as a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the equivalent of T.

clue.text: Express disapproval with mass roar

parts.note: to boo is to show disapproval by jeering

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers loudly in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express disapproval' looks like the definition but supplies the first part; the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a deep, loud resounding noise, much like a roar.

clue.text: See boiler suit troubled pioneering aviator

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

indicators.note: troubled says the letters of boiler suit are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Look at the overalls of an early airman in some distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Blériot was the French aviator who first flew across the English Channel in 1909.
